swap_risks: CRITICAL OP-AMP VS COMPARATOR TRAP: LM393DR is a comparator with open-collector output while LMV358IDR is a opamp with push-pull output. Even with identical pinouts, an open-collector comparator CANNOT pull high without an external pull-up resistor and lacks internal Miller compensation — dropping it into a linear negative-feedback op-amp circuit causes severe oscillation; conversely, using an op-amp as a comparator causes slow overdrive recovery and output saturation lag.

CRITICAL SUPPLY VOLTAGE RATING: LMV358IDR is limited to 5.5 V max (5.5 V abs max, p.5) whereas LM393DR supports up to 30 V (36 V abs max, p.4). Installing a 5.5 V CMOS op-amp on a 12 V–24 V rail causes instant breakdown.

HIGH HEADROOM / CLIPPING RISK: Rail-to-rail capability differs (LM393DR: IN=Non-RR, OUT=Non-RR vs LMV358IDR: IN=Non-RR, OUT=RR); verify input common-mode range (Vicm) and output voltage swing against ADC full-scale range.
CAUTION THERMAL MARGIN: Package θJA differs by 29% (LM393DR: 148.5 °C/W p.5 vs LMV358IDR: 207.9 °C/W p.6); re-check Tj = Ta + Pd × θJA against Tj,max.
engineering_verdict: LM393DR (Texas Instruments, SOIC-8) and LMV358IDR (Texas Instruments, SOIC-8) are Level 2 Functional / Tuning Required replacements: while the footprint is physically compatible, engineering review and passive/circuit adjustments are mandatory due to device kind / output stage mismatch (comparator/open-collector vs opamp/push-pull); supply voltage Vs,max drops >20%; rail-to-rail input/output swing differs. Key datasheet deltas: device type is comparator (open-collector) vs opamp (push-pull), supply limit is 30 V (p.4) vs 5.5 V (p.5), max Vos is 5 mV (p.8) vs 7 mV (p.7), input bias current is 25000 pA (p.8) vs 15000 pA (p.7), and Iq/ch is 225 µA (p.8) vs 105 µA (p.7). Always validate pinout orientation (TOP_VIEW p.3 vs TOP_VIEW p.3), thermal margin (θJA 148.5 vs 207.9 °C/W), and official manufacturer datasheets on hardware prototypes before production release.
